newsitem.title: USA: Chevron to seek judge's recusal in Texas case.
newsitem.headline: Chevron to seek judge's recusal in Texas case.

text.p: Chevron Corp attorneys plan to ask a federal judge to recuse himself from an ongoing trial, the Houston Chronicle reported on Friday.

The trial is to decide if pollution left behind from oil pits on a property formerly owned by Chevron seeped into water pipes and caused widespread illnesses in the black Kennedy Heights neighborhood later built on the site.
According to the newspaper, Chevron is expected to file a motion that racial comments by Judge Kenneth Hoyt, who is black, make a fair trial impossible.

Chevron said Judge Hoyt was considering excluding from the trial an Arthritis Foundation booklet that concludes African-Americans are more susceptible to lupus than the general population "because white people wrote it," the Houston Chronicle reported.
Attorneys in the case declined comment, citing a gag order in the case, and Hoyt was not immediately available for comment.

In a draft of the recusal motion, Chevron said Hoyt's personal views on race have prevented the company from getting a fair trial in a case in which plaintiffs' attorney John O'Quinn charged the company with "environmental racism", the Chronicle reported.
Hoyt in one conversation said physical differences among the races were a product of their environment, the Chronicle said, reporting from a draft of Chevron's motion.

The plaintiffs allege land containing oil pits operated from 1921 to 1927 by Gulf Oil, which Chevron later acquired, was sold to a developer planning to build a "Negro" neighborhood. The suit alleges pollutants intentionally left behind seeped into water pipes causing lupus and other diseases.
